title: [storage] How long the disk lasts is measured from every grower that persists: the archive, Claude Code's transcripts and the database
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/storage.rs (`record`, `Sampler`: the loop's `host.storage` sample), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/storage.rs (`growth`, `sizes`, `with_free`, `report`), crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs (`HOST_STORAGE`, `host_storage`, `database_size`) and web/src/resources.ts (`storageView`).

The problem (owner via lead-mac and rev-e, 2026-11-12 13:50; sync/roadmap-effects.md, Storage, "Days until the disk is full"; sync/notes-guardrails-rev-e.md, item 7). The storage north star is the number of days until the disk is full, at the measured growth of what persists. The page computes it from the transcript archive alone (objective 065). But Claude Code's transcripts (~/.claude/projects, never deleted) and the live database grow too, so the figure says the disk lasts longer than it does. Its range, 180 days or more, is set only once this is fixed. Workspaces are left out: they are checkouts that come and go with tasks, and the card already shows their total on its own row (rev-e agreed).

Required behaviour.
(a) The loop's `host.storage` sample also records `database_bytes`, the live database's size (pg_database_size), read as health.storage.database reads it. A sample whose database size cannot be read leaves the field out and is still written.
(b) `health.storage` on `GET /api/fleet`:
- keeps `growth_bytes_per_day` as the archive's alone, as today;
- adds `growth_parts` {archive, projects, database}, in bytes a day. Each part is measured as 065 measures the archive's: its size in this answer, less its size in the oldest sample of the last 7 days that carries it, over the days between, rounded down; null without such a sample at least a day old. The archive's part comes from `archive_bytes`, Claude Code's transcripts' from `projects_bytes`, and the database's from `database_bytes` against this answer's database bytes. Older samples without `database_bytes` still count for the other two parts. `growth_parts.archive` equals `growth_bytes_per_day`.
- adds `persistent_growth_bytes_per_day`, the parts' sum, null while any part is null;
- `days_left` becomes free_bytes over the persistent growth, rounded down, and null without one above 0.
(c) web/src/resources.ts `storageView`: `lasts` reads "about <days> days at the growth of the archive, Claude Code's transcripts and the database". The archive's row still says the archive's own growth ("grows about <size> a day"). The module keeps loading with node alone.
(d) If objective 083 (`growth_from_ms`, "measured from") is in the tree, it keeps its meaning for the archive's row. The page's "How long the disk lasts" line may say "not measured yet" while the persistent growth is null.

Expected on live after the deploy (not a defect): no sample before the deploy carries `database_bytes`, so the database's part, the persistent growth and with them days left ("How long the disk lasts") are blank for about a day. They appear by themselves once the first sample with the database's size is a day old. The archive's row keeps its growth all along.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/085.sh, on 065's world: an archive of 12 MiB, Claude Code's projects of 1 MiB and workspaces of 2 MiB. Samples are seeded before the loop starts: one 3 days ago in the old shape (archive 9 MiB, projects 0.25 MiB, no database_bytes), and one 2 days ago (archive 10 MiB, projects 0.5 MiB, and database_bytes 8 MiB below the database's size when seeded). Checks:
- (1) The loop's first sample carries the archive and the projects as before, and a database_bytes between pg_database_size read before the loop starts and after the sample (1% slack).
- (2) Through `GET /api/fleet`:
  - growth_bytes_per_day is the archive's 3 MiB over 3 days, and growth_parts.archive is the same;
  - growth_parts.projects is 0.75 MiB over 3 days, from the old-shape sample;
  - growth_parts.database is this answer's database bytes less the 2-day-old sample's, over 2 days;
  - persistent_growth_bytes_per_day is their sum, and days_left is free_bytes over it.
- (3) Under node, storageView's lasts has the new words, and the archive's row keeps its own growth.
It fails with 1 on c3c53a80: no database_bytes, no growth_parts, days_left over the archive alone, and the old words.

The same commit amends 065.sh's days-left checks so they accept both rules. Its seed has no database_bytes, so under this objective its days_left is null. 084.sh already accepts a null days left (0d1a0939).

The product reason. Days left is the figure that says when the host runs out of disk, and today it overstates that by counting only one of the three things that never shrink. Monitoring only: no gate, integrator or deploy step reads it.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (065, 074, 083 and 084 read the storage figures) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: a sampler test that the sample carries database_bytes, a spawn-postgres test that the oldest sample carrying a field is found through the real store (an older sample without it is passed over), a serve/storage unit test of the parts and their sum (a part null, a part negative), and a web/test case of the new words.
